What to judge: `IndexInputBindingForStoreIn` now returns the federated-material binding through `keptIndexMaterialDigest`, a process cache (`keptCache`, bounded at 256) keyed by `indexMaterialStateKey`. The key covers the engine version and the project, and for the operation's root and each root the explicit resolver authorizes: HEAD, `git status --porcelain=v1 -z --untracked-files=all --ignore-submodules=none`, and the bytes (or link target, dir or missing marker) of every path the status lists. There is no key without an explicit resolver or past 4,096 listed paths. Git runs with GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0, LC_ALL=C and LANGUAGE=C. Judge whether the key misses any input the material reads. Candidates: an ignored file, a file in a nested repository, a submodule's own working tree, a root the material reads that the resolver does not list. Judge whether parsing the status output is correct (renames and copies carry two paths), whether a failed build is never kept, and whether the read view's closure and audit stay sound when the material is not read in this operation. Measured on harne8 (clean clone at cc7780b1, pose-dist at 7e46b1e), two `pose_closeout_state` calls on one MCP server: without the cache 138 s and 136 s, with it 138 s and 11 s, terminal in all four.
